title: Primary and surrogate keys
objectives: A surrogate identity gives a record a stable internal reference while a scoped unique constraint protects a business key such as a tenant-specific email address.
The identity is a stable internal key; the tenant/email uniqueness rule models the actual business relationship and can evolve independently of the primary key.
securityBoundary: Surrogate keys do not by themselves enforce tenancy. Queries, composite foreign keys and application authorization still need tenant context.
